propositions: The N=3000 integration benchmark performs 6,000 subprocess-backed git config user.name lookups (one per append_event call) consuming 47.79s cumulatively, when only one lookup is needed per import session.

The batch_stage_and_commit path calls sweep_stale_staging once per new CREATE ticket (3,000 times) rescanning the same staging root repeatedly within a batch boundary, consuming 15.94s and 375,876 owner checks, when only one sweep per bounded batch is needed.

An import-scoped, fallback-keyed author cache with copy-on-write semantics can reduce redundant lookups while preserving live per-call behavior for interactive/direct writes and maintaining the existing user.email/identity invalidation semantics.
A single stale-staging sweep on the first new-ticket prepare in each bounded batch eliminates rescans while preserving crash-resume, rollback, atomic staging/publish, and all per-event validation.

The locked N=3000 contract (3,000 creates, 6,000 events, exactly 24 commits, >=10x reduction) must remain unchanged; identical-harness A/B testing demonstrates 60.8s (78.8%) wall-time delta is attributable solely to author-lookup and sweep-scan mechanisms, not serialization or commit-count rules.
